card.name: Main verb right after its subject
card.fires_on: A main verb or verb-like word (to, is, become, arises, start) placed right after its subject, often after an opening phrase about time or history. The verb is about to be followed by its complement.

modes.label: Present-tense verb after subject
modes.description: A plain present-tense verb such as is, become, arises, or start follows its subject.
modes.example: computers<< become>> out of date' at an astounding rate

modes.label: Existential or idiom verb
modes.description: A word like 'to' or 'is' sits in a phrase such as 'comes to play' or 'there is'.
modes.example: comes<< to>> play each and every football season

card.writes: It nudges the model toward past-tense action verbs like took, did, held (especially in Chinese), and away from words like shortly and peacefully.
card.plain: It marks the spot right after a sentence's subject where the main verb is expected to give what happened.
